text:
Let $α\in \left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$ be fixed. If the integral

$\int \frac{\tan x+\tan α}{\tan x-\tan α}dx$ = A(x) cos 2$α$ + B(x) sin 2$α$ + C,  where C is a

constant of integration, then the functions A(x) and B(x) are respectively :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve the given integral, first we simplify the expression in the integral as follows :

$\int \frac{\tan x+\tan α}{\tan x-\tan α}dx=\int \frac{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}+\frac{\sin α}{\cos α}}{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}-\frac{\sin α}{\cos α}}dx$ 

Simplifying further, this becomes :

$\int \frac{\sin x\cos α+\sin α\cos x}{\sin x\cos α-\sin α\cos x}dx$ 

By using the formula for sin(a + b) = sin a cos b + cos a sin b and sin(a - b) = sin a cos b - cos a sin b, we get :

$\int \frac{\sin (x+α)}{\sin (x-α)}dx$ 

Now, let's use the substitution method. Let t = x - α, therefore x = t + α and dx = dt. Substituting these values into the integral, we get :

= $\int \frac{\sin (t+2α)}{\sin t}dt$ 

$\begin{array}{l} =\int \dfrac{\sin t\cos 2α+\sin 2α\cos t}{\sin t}dt \\  \\ =\int \left (\cos 2α+\sin 2α\dfrac{\cos t}{\sin t}\right )dt \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =t(\cos 2α)+(\sin 2α)\log _{e}|\sin t|+C \\  \\ =(x-α)\cos 2α+(\sin 2α)\log _{e}|\sin (x-α)|+C \\  \\ =A(x)\cos 2α+B(x)\sin 2α+C\text{(given)} \end{array}$

Now on comparing, we get

$A(x)=x-α\text{and}B(x)=\log _{e}|\sin (x-α)|$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
If $α$, $β$ and $γ$ are three consecutive terms of a non-constant G.P. such that the equations $α$x
$^{2}$
 + 2$β$x + $γ$ = 0 and
$x^{2}$
 + x – 1 = 0 have a common root, then $α$($β$ + $γ$) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the common ratio of G.P is r

Then the equation of  $αx^{2}+2βx+γ=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $αx^{2}+2αrx+αr^{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2} + 2rx + r^{2} = 0 ........(i)$

Equation (i) and $x^{2} + x - 1 = 0 ......... (ii)$ has a common root.

Now (i) - (ii) $\Rightarrow$ $(2r-1)x + (r^{2}+1) = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ x = $\frac{-\left (r^{2}+1\right )}{2r-1}$ ....... (iii)

Now putting (iii) in equation (ii) 

$\Rightarrow$ $(r^{2}+1)^{2} - (r^{2}+1) (2r - 1) -  (2r - 1)^{2} = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ $r^{4} - 2r^{3} - r^{2} + 2r + 1 = 0 .......... (iv)$

dividing equation (iv) by $r^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $r^{2} - 2r - 1 +$ $\frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{r^{2}}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (r-\frac{1}{r}\right )^{2}-2\left (r-\frac{1}{r}\right )+1=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (r-\frac{1}{r}-r\right )^{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{r^{2}-1}{r}=1$ $\Rightarrow$ $r^{2} = 1 + r$

Now $α$($β$ + $γ$) $\Rightarrow$ $α$($α$r + $αr^{2})$

 $\Rightarrow$ $α^{2}r(1+r)$   [$\because$  $r^{2} = 1 + r$]

$\Rightarrow$ $α^{2}r.r^{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $(αr)(αr^{2})$ $\Rightarrow$ $βγ$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
A person throws two fair dice. He wins Rs. 15 for throwing a doublet (same numbers on the two dice), wins
Rs. 12 when the throw results in the sum of 9, and loses Rs. 6 for any other outcome on the throw. Then the
expected gain/loss (in Rs.) of the person is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When two dice are thrown then sample space will {(1, 1), (2, 2) ....... (6, 6)} contain total 36 elements number of cases.

Then the expectation will be $\frac{6}{36}\times 15+\frac{4}{36}\times 12-\frac{26}{36}\times 6$

$\frac{90+48-156}{36}=-\frac{1}{2}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ loss

text: An ellipse, with foci at (0, 2) and (0, –2) and minor axis of length 4, passes through which of the following points?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1(a<b)$ is the equation of ellipse, foci $(0,\pm 2)$

Given 2a = 4 $\Rightarrow$ a = 2

$e^{2} = 1 -$ $\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}$ $\Rightarrow$ $b^{2}e^{2} = b^{2} - a^{2}$

$4 = b^{2} - 4$

$b^{2} = 8$

$\because$ equation of ellipse is $\frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{y^{2}}{8}=1$

then it passes through $\left (\sqrt{2},2\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
A straight line L at a distance of 4 units from the origin makes positive intercepts on the coordinate axes and
the perpendicular from the origin to this line makes an angle of $60^{o}$ with the line x + y = 0. Then an equation
of the line L is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Since $L$ is at distance 4 from the origin and makes positive intercepts on both axes, its normal form is

$x\cos θ+y\sin θ=4,0^{\circ }<θ<90^{\circ }$

where $θ$ is the inclination of the perpendicular from the origin to $L$.

The line $x+y=0$ has inclination $135^{\circ }$. The perpendicular makes an angle of $60^{\circ }$ with it when the difference of inclinations is $60^{\circ }$ or $180^{\circ }-60^{\circ }=120^{\circ }$, so within $0^{\circ }<θ<90^{\circ }$:

$θ=135^{\circ }-60^{\circ }=75^{\circ }\text{or}θ=135^{\circ }-120^{\circ }=15^{\circ }$

Using $\cos 75^{\circ }=\sin 15^{\circ }=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2\sqrt{2}}$ and $\sin 75^{\circ }=\cos 15^{\circ }=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}$, $θ=75^{\circ }$ gives

$(\sqrt{3}-1)x+(\sqrt{3}+1)y=8\sqrt{2}$

which is option (D), and $θ=15^{\circ }$ gives

$(\sqrt{3}+1)x+(\sqrt{3}-1)y=8\sqrt{2}$

which is option (C). Both lines are at distance 4 from the origin, have positive intercepts and satisfy the angle condition.

Options (A) and (B) correspond to $θ=60^{\circ }$ and $θ=30^{\circ }$, whose perpendiculars make $75^{\circ }$ with $x+y=0$.

Hence, the correct options are (C) and (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
A value of $α$ such that

$\int\limits _{α}^{α+1}\frac{dx}{(x+α)(x+α+1)}=\log _{e}\left (\frac{9}{8}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\int\limits _{α}^{α+1}\frac{dx}{(x+α)(x+α+1)}$

Let x + $α$ = t  and dx = dt

$I=\int\limits _{2α}^{2α+1}\frac{dt}{t(t+1)}=\int\limits _{2α}^{2α+1}\left (\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{t+1}\right )dt$

$\Rightarrow (\ln t-\ln (t+1))|_{2α}^{2α+1}=\ln \left (\frac{t}{t+1}\right )|_{2α}^{2α+1}$

$\Rightarrow \ln \left (\frac{2α+1}{2α+2}\right )-\ln \left (\frac{2α}{2α+1}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \ln \left (\frac{2α+1}{2α+2}\times \frac{2α+1}{2α}\right )=\ln \left (\frac{9}{8}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{(2α+1)^{2}}{(2α+2)}=\frac{9α}{4}$

$4(4α^{2}+1+4α)=18α^{2}+18α$

$\Rightarrow 2α^{2}+2α-4=0$

$\Rightarrow α^{2}+α-2=0$

$\Rightarrow (α+2)(α-1)=0$

$α$ = 1 or $α$ = -2

text:
The term independent of x in the expansion of

$\left (\frac{1}{60}-\frac{x^{8}}{81}\right ).\left (2x^{2}-\frac{3}{x^{2}}\right )^{6}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given expression = $\left (\frac{1}{60}-\frac{x^{8}}{81}\right ).\left (2x^{2}-\frac{3}{x^{2}}\right )^{6}$

= $\frac{1}{60}\left (2x^{2}-\frac{3}{x^{2}}\right )^{6}-\frac{x^{8}}{81}\left (2x^{2}-\frac{3}{x^{2}}\right )^{6}$

So its general term is

$T_{r + 1} =$ $\frac{1}{60}{}^{6}C_{r}\left (2x^{2}\right )^{6-r}\left (-\frac{3}{x^{2}}\right )^{r}-\frac{x^{8}}{81}{}^{6}C_{r}\left (2x^{2}\right )^{6-r}\left (-\frac{3}{x^{2}}\right )^{r}$

= $\frac{1}{60}{}^{6}C_{r}(2)^{6-r}(-3)^{r}x^{12-4r}-\frac{1}{81}{}^{6}C_{r}(2)^{6-r}(-3)^{r}x^{20-4r}$  .....(i)

For this term to be independent of x, put r = 3 in
$1^{st}$ part and r = 5 in $2^{nd}$ part.

So from (i) the term independent of
 x = $\frac{1}{60}\times 2^{3}\times (-3)^{3}\times {}^{6}C_{3}+\left (-\frac{1}{81}\right )(2)(-3)^{5}\times {}^{6}C_{5}$

= -72 + 36 = -36
